name: Australia

outcome.intro: After studying this section, a student will know the general location, climate, and styles of wine produced in Australia's most important wine regions.
outcome.certified: After studying this section, a candidate will be know the specific locations, climates, and principal grape varieties of Australia's most important wine regions and the difference between bulk wine regions and premium wine regions. A Certified Sommelier will have the ability to describe Barossa/McLaren Vale Shiraz, recognize iconic producers, and be able to recommend and sell food pairings with Australian wines to a guest.

rows.intro: Southern Hemisphere, the size of continental United States.
Hot, dry interior, cooler near coast.; Cool maritime to warm Mediterranean to hot and arid.
Elevation in South Australia, currents from Antarctica.
Concept of blending across regions for volume.; 100+ year old vines exist.; Irrigation is necessary in the country interior.; Best vineyards are near the cooler coast.
Traditional: Blending across regions, American oak; Modern: Single GI/site, French oak
GI: Refers to a geographic place of origin only, no other additional laws.; 85% labeling required for grape variety, vintage, and origin.

Geographic Indications (GIs): Indicates Geographical location only.; Australia, State, Zone, Region, Sub-Region; *More specificity as the region gets smaller. No need to memorize which are Zones vs. Regions but know this system exists.; *South Eastern Australia Super GI (high-volume)

New South Wales GI; Victoria GI; South Australia GI; Western Australia GI; South Eastern Australia GI: Riverina GI, Murray Darling GI; Victoria GI: Yarra Valley GI; South Australia GI: Barossa Valley GI, McLaren Vale GI, Clare Valley GI, Eden Valley GI; Western Australia GI: Margaret River GI
rows.certified: Tasmania GI; New South Wales GI: Hunter Valley GI; South Australia GI: Coonawarra GI

rows.intro: First vines planted in 1788 (near Sydney), industry moved west after phylloxera (quarantine), sweet/fortified wines dominated until late 20th Century, purchased French company that invented Stelvin closure, Yellow Tail business model.

rows.certified: Ripe Shiraz with intense grilled or barbecued meat. Use Clare or Eden Riesling like New Zealand Sauvignon Blanc. Yarra Pinot Noir parallels Willamette Valley Pinot Noir. Yarra Chardonnay works like Sonoma Coast Chardonnay. Margaret River Bordeaux blends are elegant like wines from Bordeaux.
